research_question: Does cross-episode Actor state carry (time_step_counter and semantically coupled decoder K/V cache) causally change Actor hidden states, logits, or actions for the same teacher-forced current-episode input sequence when rollover timing differs?
hypothesis: H-RESET: a valid carried Actor state package that shifts rollover timing causes reproducible hidden/logit divergence and may cause action divergence under identical teacher-forced inputs.
competing_explanation: H-RESET-INERT: after a semantically valid reset/carry construction and deterministic replay, the same input sequence yields equivalent Actor outputs across rollover, so retained state is an engineering irregularity rather than an active policy mechanism on the tested path.
reference: 02｜SafeVLA Gate B FAIL: Actor/Reward/Cost decoder counters and K/V cache persist across episode reset; historical short mask-isolation test matched at fresh-episode start but did not causally test later max_steps=500 rollover. Historical premature-end probability audits are complete and no further p(end)-only experiment is authorized.
repeat_or_treatment: P0 static state-carrier audit; P1 explicit RESET_STATE_FIX with OFF official and ON Actor-only correct reset plus model-level A/A OFF equivalence; P2 deterministic offline CLEAN-START versus valid CARRY-300 stress replay on the same teacher-forced real B0 Actor input sequence. Maximum four live episodes only to acquire a fixed input trace or A/A smoke.
unique_variable: Initial Actor model-side episode state package / rollover position. All teacher-forced Actor inputs, weights, masks, recorded previous-action inputs and offline RNG draws are held fixed.
fixed_conditions: No PT-Guard, Stop Gate, steering, reranking, action rewrite or success-oracle gate
RESET_STATE_FIX=0 must be model-level A/A equivalent to untouched official code on identical saved inputs and RNG
RESET_STATE_FIX=1 resets only the Actor episode-local state proven necessary by the static audit; if Actor-only isolation is impossible, return R4
No formal Probe, size analysis, 200-task evaluation or three-checkpoint comparison
Offline stress replay remains teacher-forced after any predicted-action divergence
Primary action comparison is argmax; optional sampled comparison uses common random numbers
Treatment code is not committed to the B0 execution branch; review uses reset_fix.patch and research-loop handoff artifacts
metrics: A/A OFF hidden/logit/probability/greedy/sampled equivalence on identical inputs and RNG
Per-step Actor counter and cache write/start position
Distance from first rollover event to first divergence
expected_result: Either establish a reproducible state-carrier -> Actor distribution/action pathway around rollover (R1/R2), or substantially downgrade H-RESET after a valid no-difference result (R3).
falsifying_result: H-RESET as an active policy mechanism is weakened if semantically valid CLEAN-START and CARRY-300 replays remain equivalent through the rollover-relevant region on the fixed real input sequence.
alternative_explanations: A fabricated counter value without compatible cache contents would create an invalid treatment
CUDA numerical nondeterminism may masquerade as tiny divergence unless within-condition replay stability is verified
One stress sequence may not generalize to population-level performance
Counter+cache package causality does not separately attribute counter versus cache
Model-level action divergence does not by itself prove SR impact
stop_conditions: Static audit cannot define a valid Actor-only reset package
RESET_STATE_FIX=0 differs from untouched official model replay on identical inputs/RNG
Logger/instrumentation changes forward count, RNG, inputs, history or environment semantics
A valid >=220-decision fixed input sequence cannot be obtained within four live episodes
CARRY-300 cannot be constructed with semantically compatible cache state
Within-condition offline replay is not stable enough for comparison
Execution would expand to Probe, Stop Gate, 200-task evaluation, size analysis or multi-checkpoint performance comparison
